samples.summary: Canonical subsystem doc still describes the infra/carry-forward discriminator as "API/quota error" only — pool exhaustion is now part of the never-ran class and isn't recorded there
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1657-1675 ("Infra errors are excluded from carry-forward. A lens that hit an API/quota outage (e.g. a 429 session limit) never reviewed…") and :1811-1822 ("When EVERY blocking lens fails on an API error the panel marks an infraError…") are the repo's only prose record of this mechanism. The diff changes the producer's rule from `kind === "api-error"` to `sessionNeverRan` (`api-error` ∪ `pool-exhausted`) and adds a new closed-vocabulary code `POOL_EXHAUSTED`, but neither section is updated, so the doc now under-describes the classification that the whole carry-forward guarantee hangs on. CONTRIBUTING.md:11 exempts bug fixes from a *new* design doc, which is why this is minor rather than major — but the doc it would fold into already exists and documents exactly this rule.

samples.summary: Tests for the two new review-panel.mjs exports live in prior-findings.test.mjs and redact.test.mjs, not in review-panel.test.mjs
samples.evidence: `allSamplesFailedError`/`lensFailureSummary` are exercised from prior-findings.test.mjs:5-28 and `lensInfraReason` from redact.test.mjs:15,343-372, while scripts/agent/review-panel.test.mjs is the home-of-record suite for that module (it already covers panelEntry, unionSamples, classifyResult). The producer-to-consumer round trip justifies the prior-findings placement, but there is now no review-panel.test.mjs coverage of either new export, so a reader looking for the panel's infra-classification tests will not find them where the module's other tests are.
searchedFor: grep infra in scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs and review-panel.test.mjs
